newsitem.title: USA: Calif. budget reserve should get boost - Treasurer.
newsitem.headline: Calif. budget reserve should get boost - Treasurer.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong said on Wednesday the state should increase its budget reserve but does not need as large a cushion as other states because of its diverse economy.
"I would like to see, in principle, a stronger reserve," Fong told reporters in a conference call from New York, where he was meeting with major credit rating agencies.

"If we continue sustained economic growth, which is being predicted, I think we can make an argument that next year, the governor would continue the trend upwards, and put more money aside for the rainy day," Fong said.

California Gov. Pete Wilson's $66.6 billion 1997-1998 budget proposal includes a reserve of $553 million. The reserve has drawn fire from some Wall Street and state budget analysts for being too small.
In a report last month, California's Legislative Analyst said Wilson's modest reserve was an improvement but was relatively small compared to the size of the budget.
While agreeing with analysts that the state should increase its budget reserve, Fong told reporters on Wednesday that California does not need as large of a cushion as many other smaller states.
"I don't believe that the rating agencies are being realistic in putting California into the same standard as other states that do require, I think, a more significant reserve," Fong said.
"I've argued with them (rating agency officials) that you know you don't need as strong as a reserve because our economy is broader, wider, deeper than any other state," he added.
